findings.title: Node outbound request deadlines do not cancel the transport
findings.observed: The Node provider passes timeout to request options but registers no timeout teardown handler. Callers may race the returned promise against timeLimit; the seed setup call relies only on the request option. The browser sibling explicitly aborts its fetch.
findings.expected_boundary: Deadline expiry must end the underlying I/O and settle the operation, not only stop one caller waiting.
findings.failure_mechanism: Promise rejection is disconnected from socket/request lifetime. The Node request is not destroyed when the wrapper expires; setup has no wrapper deadline on the seed call. Actual socket leakage/hang was not reproduced.
findings.break_it_angle: Use a local fake peer that accepts and stalls; inspect request closure after deadline and repeat without restarting the client. Also exercise the setup seed path.
findings.impact: A stalled peer may leave setup pending or accumulate live network work after callers report timeouts. No EMFILE, OOM or once-per-minute leak was observed; connection behavior and the sync mutex must be considered in a drill.

mitigation.minimal_repair: Add deadline-driven cancellation at the transport owner, propagate abort signals, clean up timers/listeners, and handle the Node and Electron client variants explicitly.
mitigation.local_guardrail: A fake stalled peer must cause bounded rejection and connection closure, including setup seed.
mitigation.behavior_test: Repeat timeout, partial-body error, success and caller cancellation cases and assert no retained sockets or timers.

findings.title: The server log write stream lacks a local error and recovery policy
findings.observed: The file stream is opened and written without a stream-specific error listener or recovery state. The shared date rotation starts asynchronously and suppresses rotation rejection. Process error reporting does retain a console fallback.
findings.expected_boundary: Diagnostic-channel failure should be detected without depending on the same failed channel; recovery or explicit degradation should be bounded and visible.
findings.failure_mechanism: No component owns a failed file stream transition. The general error handler can report to console, but does not reopen the stream. An outage lasting for the entire process lifetime is not established: later rotation can reopen it.
findings.break_it_angle: Inject a write-stream error on a disposable path, then restore writability and examine console, UI and subsequent file output.
findings.impact: File diagnostics may be lost while the process continues. The recovered claim of total silent diagnostic loss was too strong because console output and process-level notifications exist.

mitigation.minimal_repair: Own write-stream errors locally, keep the console fallback, mark degradation, and define a bounded reopen/backoff policy that does not recurse through the failed logger.
mitigation.local_guardrail: Inject stream-open and mid-write errors and assert no uncaught logging recursion.
mitigation.behavior_test: Restore writability and prove either recovery or a persistent actionable degraded signal.

findings.title: An in-flight provider construction can repopulate a newly invalidated cache with old settings
findings.observed: Provider configuration changes clear a shared cache. getProvider reads a configuration, awaits creation, and then stores the resulting instance into the current cache keyed only by config ID.
findings.expected_boundary: Cache publication must remain associated with the configuration revision that created the instance.
findings.failure_mechanism: Request A captures settings A and awaits a dynamic factory. Settings change; request B resets/builds cache B. If A finishes later, it can insert an A instance into cache B, while cachedProvidersSource still records settings B. A later lookup for that ID returns stale settings until another invalidation.
findings.break_it_angle: Defer a first construction, edit the same provider ID, complete the new lookup, then release the old factory and inspect subsequent resolution. This interleaving was reasoned from source, not executed.
findings.impact: A saved provider edit may not take effect consistently; calls can continue using the old endpoint/configuration. Race frequency and live provider effects are unmeasured.

mitigation.minimal_repair: Bind cache entries and in-flight construction to a source/generation fingerprint; publish only if that generation is still current. Define whether the initiating request may finish using its original configuration.
mitigation.local_guardrail: Use deferred factories to reproduce both completion orders across a configuration change.
mitigation.behavior_test: Assert subsequent lookups always use the current revision and that a stale completion cannot overwrite it.

findings.title: Standalone worker failure does not settle restore waiters
findings.observed: Restore requests use a separate restores map. Worker error handling rejects pending API requests, but does not reject/clear restore waiters. FATAL_ERROR displays an overlay and returns; only RESTORE_RESULT settles a restore.
findings.expected_boundary: A fatal worker transition should settle every in-flight operation it owns, even when the global UI already reports a crash.
findings.failure_mechanism: The request families have divergent failure cleanup. A worker that stops before RESTORE_RESULT leaves the restore promise and associated callback rooted without a terminal result.
findings.break_it_angle: Start a restore on a fake worker, then emit its error/fatal event instead of RESTORE_RESULT. Do not kill a real database worker for this check.
findings.impact: The caller may never receive its terminal restore outcome. Severity stays Low because the global overlay is visible; this is not evidence that restore data is corrupt or that every failure is silent.

mitigation.minimal_repair: Centralize worker-failure settlement across pending, restore, download and save families. Preserve the global error overlay and report that the operation outcome is uncertain where appropriate.
mitigation.local_guardrail: Use the fake worker to assert restore rejection and callback-map cleanup on every fatal event family.
mitigation.behavior_test: Verify a late response cannot settle a replacement operation or report old work as successful.

findings.title: Repository instructions name a different origin and checkout topology

evidence.quote:
### Opening a PR

`git push -u origin <branch>` then `gh pr create --base main --title … --body-file <file>`. There is no PR template in `.github/`, so the body is yours to shape.

- **`origin` is `TriliumNext/Trilium`** — the working directory is named `Notes` and ~19 contributor forks are configured as remotes, so neither the path nor the remote list names the target. `gh` resolves it from `remote.origin.gh-resolved`, already set, so `--repo` is redundant; `upstream` is the archived `zadam/trilium` and is never a base.

findings.observed: The checked-in instructions say origin is TriliumNext/Trilium, the working directory is Notes and roughly nineteen contributor remotes exist. Read-only Git inspection shows this checkout is Trilium with only origin at cephalopod-ai/Trilium.
findings.expected_boundary: Repository operation instructions should separate upstream examples from observed fork-specific destinations.
findings.failure_mechanism: A hardcoded environment assertion is phrased as current operational truth. It can misdirect target selection in an agent or human workflow that fails to re-read Git state.
findings.break_it_angle: Compare the instruction paragraph to git remote -v and git rev-parse --show-toplevel in this checkout.
findings.impact: Misleading operational guidance for this fork. No wrong-target push was observed; the earlier integration used the actual remote correctly.

checked_boundaries.title: Backup mutual exclusion
checked_boundaries.conclusion: Both backupNow and backupAs enter the same process-wide mutex; a mutex excludes every acquire, not just callers named sync. The recovered overlap-corruption allegation is rejected.

checked_boundaries.title: Scheduled backup retention shape
checked_boundaries.conclusion: Daily, weekly and monthly use fixed backup names; the alleged daily timestamped-file accumulation does not occur on this path. This says nothing about user-named manual backups.

checked_boundaries.title: Backup publication
checked_boundaries.conclusion: The container path renames after writing and removes snapshot/part files in finally. Crash durability/fsync and actual restore correctness were not drilled.

checked_boundaries.title: Branch route transaction owner
checked_boundaries.conclusion: The synchronous HTTP wrapper supplies the SQL transaction; inline route code alone does not prove non-atomicity. Standalone transaction equivalence is not certified by this one trace.

checked_boundaries.title: Fatal server boot handling
checked_boundaries.conclusion: startApplication awaits initialization/startup and catches failures with process.exit(1). Listen errors also call platform.crash. The recovered speculative pre-listening escape example is not established.

checked_boundaries.title: Portable host-provider absence
checked_boundaries.conclusion: An unregistered host provider produces an explicit named build-unavailable error. It does not silently fall back to a different provider.

checked_boundaries.title: ACP request/pool cleanup
checked_boundaries.conclusion: Requests clear deadline timers when resolved/rejected; pool release arms an idle reaper. This held sample does not cover every child-process shutdown race.

checked_boundaries.title: Claude warm-session lifetime
checked_boundaries.conclusion: The pool has an idle timeout and closes old idle sessions when over its warm-session target. Busy sessions are intentionally not evicted, so this is not proof of an admission cap on active chats.

checked_boundaries.title: Native session completion truth
checked_boundaries.conclusion: The native provider persists a pending mapping before prompting and requires end_turn before clearing it and emitting done. Interrupted output is not automatically reclassified as complete.

checked_boundaries.title: Native cancellation cleanup
checked_boundaries.conclusion: The finally path detaches/releases the lease and removes turn and abort listeners; incomplete scoped mappings are revoked.

checked_boundaries.title: Dynamic model discovery
checked_boundaries.conclusion: Listing uses a bounded fetch and a TTL/in-flight cache; failures are differentiated from unsupported listing. No live model-retirement or pricing-freshness claim is made.

checked_boundaries.title: MCP result semantics and transport teardown
checked_boundaries.conclusion: Tool error results set isError, and response close closes transport/server. Schema/protocol conformance beyond this sample remains unexercised.

checked_boundaries.title: Standalone ownership
checked_boundaries.conclusion: The browser uses an exclusive Web Lock for its database-owning tab and rejects follower restore requests. The no-Web-Locks fallback is a retained platform assumption.

checked_boundaries.title: Widget unmount cleanup
checked_boundaries.conclusion: The ordinary dispose helper explicitly unmounts the Preact root. That is distinct from handling a render exception.

checked_boundaries.title: Source validation policy
checked_boundaries.conclusion: CLAUDE.md calls for scoped tests and one typecheck, with full suites left to CI; the server uses fork isolation and has an explicit worker limit. No unsupported recommendation to serialize all tests or remove cross-runtime core runs is made.

evidence.quote:
- **Never run ESLint** (`dev:linter-check`, `dev:linter-fix`, `npx eslint`) — it dies with an out-of-memory error, so a run tells you nothing. CI does not lint either — there is no `eslint`/`linter-check` step anywhere in `.github/workflows/`, so lint findings never block a merge; the gates are `pnpm typecheck` and the per-package `test --coverage` runs. (`packages/*` is ignored by the ESLint config anyway.)
- **Never run `pnpm test:all`, `test:parallel`, `test:sequential`, or a whole-package `coverage`** during development — CI runs them on every push. Run the **narrowest** suite that covers what you touched: `pnpm --filter <pkg> test <pattern>` (Vitest treats the trailing argument as a substring filter over spec paths). Core specs need **two** runs, server and standalone (see Testing). Only reach for a full suite if the user asks or wants a final check.
- **Typecheck with `pnpm typecheck`, not a raw `tsc`** — it resolves the project references a hand-written `tsc -p …` gets wrong, and is far cheaper than a test suite. Still, run it **once, after a piece of work is finished** — not after every edit: it builds the project references, and repeating it is a common way to lose minutes across a session. Two ways its output misleads: the incremental build does not recheck the files that use an ambient `.d.ts` (`types-lib.d.ts`) after it changes — delete `apps/client/dist/*.tsbuildinfo` (gitignored) before trusting the result; and a dependent project (`tsconfig.spec.json`, `apps/build-docs`) is checked only once the app project compiles, so its errors appear only after the app's are fixed, and some vanish with them.
